Landscape 16:9 (1536x1024) scene for an animated explainer video. Loose blue-ink pen sketch on a page of college-ruled notebook paper with pale blue rules and a row of punched holes down the left edge, quick lively outlines with a little scribbled shading and the odd stray construction line left in. A green felt-tip accent is used ONLY on the main character's scarf and on one or two tiny details per scene; everything else is blue ink on the white page. Supporting people are sketched in the same blue ink with ordinary proportions, oval faces, a nose, proper eyes with lids and their own hair and clothes, never the main character's bean-shaped head or button eyes, and never in green. Anyone who appears in more than one scene keeps the same hair, clothes and build; phones, cars, furniture and fashion fit the time the story is set in. Figures stay separate and never overlap or blend into each other, the same people who walk into a diagram walk out of it, and charts or size comparisons keep exactly the proportions the narration gives. Scene: A paper boat drifts across a puddle beside a kerb, with two small ripples behind it. Use the attached sheet only as a reference for the pen style; the main character is NOT in this scene unless the scene text says so. No text, letters or words anywhere in the image. Keep the composition simple and readable, main subject centered with some empty paper around the edges. No logos, brand names or real people's likenesses. Everything is drawn the right way up and facing the way the scene describes (screens and pages face whoever is reading them). Every hand has exactly five fingers; no extra or merged limbs.
